answer: A deposit that unlocks only after a long season of real work makes fake identities expensive. Each agent posts a small bond to join, paid back only after verified tasks over weeks. An attacker must fund every copy and wait out the same season, so ten thousand fake agents cost ten thousand bonds and months of idle money. Honest agents pass once, like a crystal forming under pressure, while a zephyr of cheap copies blows away before reaching its zenith. The bond is time and money the attacker cannot get back.
